source_meta._title: Villagers can sell experimental enchantments without the 1.21 experiment enabled

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1 (launcher version name: 1.20.5-rc1)
stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition in a disposable single-player Creative world. Use the official launcher with snapshots enabled, no mods, no third-party datapacks, no resource packs that rename items, and all built-in experiments disabled. A Superflat world and frozen daytime are used as practical controls to make repeated villager profession changes easier; they are not stated requirements of the report.
preconditions: Install and launch exactly Minecraft: Java Edition 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1, not 1.20.5 Release Candidate 2 or the final 1.20.5 release.
Use a newly created test world rather than an important existing world because release-candidate versions can damage or convert worlds.
Leave both the Update 1.21 experiment and the Villager Trade Rebalance experiment disabled. Do not enable any other experiment or install an experimental datapack.
Use Creative mode with commands allowed so the villager, lectern, enclosure, and controlled daytime can be established without unrelated resource gathering.
Do not complete any trade with the test villager. Completing even one trade locks that villager's profession and offers, preventing the lectern-breaking reroll procedure.
The relevant mace-only enchantment names in this version are Density, Breach, and Wind Burst. Any displayed enchantment level is sufficient for identifying a matching offer.
Trade generation is random, so an unspecified number of rerolls may be required.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher. In Installations, enable historical snapshot installations, create or select an installation for 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1, and start it. If the launcher offers a separate game directory, use one dedicated to this test.
steps.exact_input: Installations -> Snapshots: enabled -> New Installation -> Version: 1.20.5-rc1 -> Play
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu loads and identifies the running version as 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1 or 1.20.5-rc1.

steps.action: From the main menu, open the single-player world list and begin creating a new world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set the world to Creative mode and turn Allow Commands or Allow Cheats on if it is presented as a separate option.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Commands/Allow Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: The creation screen shows Creative mode, with commands permitted.

steps.action: Open the world settings and select the default Superflat world type. This avoids having to locate a clear construction area and reduces the chance of unrelated village workstations being nearby.
steps.exact_input: World settings -> World Type: Superflat
steps.success_cue: The selected world type is Superflat.

steps.action: Open the Experiments screen. Confirm that Update 1.21 and Villager Trade Rebalance are both off. Do not activate any experiment before returning to the creation screen.
steps.exact_input: Experiments -> Update 1.21: OFF; Villager Trade Rebalance: OFF
steps.success_cue: No experiment is selected and the world-creation screen does not show an experimental-world warning caused by enabling an experiment.

steps.action: Create the world and wait until terrain is rendered and normal player movement responds.
steps.exact_input: Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the new world, nearby terrain is visible, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press F3 to open the debug overlay and verify the displayed client version is 1.20.5-rc1. Close the overlay with F3 after checking.
steps.exact_input: F3
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay identifies 1.20.5-rc1, and the overlay is then closed.

steps.action: Verify the world's enabled datapacks. Press T to open chat, enter the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter. Inspect the resulting enabled-pack list for any Update 1.21 or Villager Trade Rebalance pack.
steps.exact_input: /datapack list enabled
steps.success_cue: The enabled-pack output does not list an Update 1.21 experimental pack or a Villager Trade Rebalance experimental pack.

steps.action: Place the world at the beginning of villager working time. Open chat with T, execute the command exactly, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /time set 2000
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms the time was changed, and the world is in daylight.

steps.action: Freeze the daylight cycle so the villager remains in a suitable daytime schedule while trades are repeatedly rerolled. Open chat with T, execute the command exactly, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /gamerule doDaylightCycle false
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that doDaylightCycle is now false, and the sun no longer advances.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use its search field to obtain a Villager Spawn Egg, a Lectern, and enough full solid blocks for a small enclosure. Move all three item types into hotbar slots, then close the inventory with E or Esc. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen; select a slot using the number keys 1 through 9 or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E; search for "Villager Spawn Egg", "Lectern", and a full solid block
steps.success_cue: A Villager Spawn Egg, a Lectern, and enclosure blocks are present in accessible hotbar slots.

steps.action: On the flat ground, build an enclosure with an interior at least 3 blocks by 3 blocks and walls 2 blocks high. Leave the top open so the Creative-mode player can fly in and out. Do not place any lectern or other villager workstation yet.
steps.exact_input: Select the solid blocks and right-click to place them
steps.success_cue: A villager cannot walk out of the enclosure, and there is clear floor space inside for both one villager and one lectern.

steps.action: Select the Villager Spawn Egg in the hotbar. Aim at the floor inside the empty enclosure and use the egg once with right-click. Do not use the egg directly on an existing villager.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the enclosure floor once with Villager Spawn Egg selected
steps.success_cue: One adult, unemployed villager is standing inside the enclosure and cannot escape.

steps.action: Select the Lectern in the hotbar. Enter or hover over the enclosure in Creative flight, then right-click an empty floor block immediately beside the villager to place the lectern where the villager can walk up to it.
steps.exact_input: Right-click an empty floor block with Lectern selected
steps.success_cue: The lectern is placed inside the enclosure within direct walking distance of the villager.

steps.action: Wait without opening the trade screen until the villager claims the lectern and changes into a librarian. Continue only after the profession change is visible; green particles may also appear during the claim.
steps.success_cue: The adult villager is wearing the librarian profession outfit while the lectern remains accessible.

steps.action: With an empty hand or any non-interfering item selected, aim at the librarian and use right-click to open its trading interface.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the librarian
steps.success_cue: The Trading screen is open and displays the novice librarian's current trade rows.

steps.action: Inspect every currently visible novice trade without completing one. For any trade whose output is an Enchanted Book, move the pointer over the output book icon and leave it there long enough for the tooltip to appear. Read the enchantment name and level. A matching target is a tooltip named Density, Breach, or Wind Burst at any level. Do not click the trade row's execution area, supply payment items, or take an output item.
steps.exact_input: Hover the pointer over each Enchanted Book output icon
steps.success_cue: The tooltip for the current Enchanted Book offer is visible and its enchantment name can be read, while no trade has been completed.

steps.action: If none of the current offers is an Enchanted Book with Density, Breach, or Wind Burst, press Esc to close the Trading screen. If one of those names is displayed, do not close the screen; stop the reproduction sequence at step 17 and hand control to the observation subsystem.
steps.exact_input: Esc only when no target mace enchantment is present
steps.success_cue: For a non-matching roll, the player is back in the world facing the same librarian and lectern. For a matching roll, the Trading screen remains open with the pointer over the target book output.

steps.action: For a non-matching roll, select an empty hand or another suitable Creative-mode slot, aim directly at the lectern, and break it with left-click. Ensure the lectern itself, rather than an enclosure block, is removed.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the lectern
steps.success_cue: The lectern block is gone and the villager remains safely inside the enclosure.

steps.action: Wait until the untraded villager releases the destroyed lectern and visibly loses the librarian profession. Do not continue merely because the lectern has disappeared. If the villager remains a librarian, verify that no trade was completed and that there is no second lectern nearby, then continue waiting while the frozen daytime remains active.
steps.success_cue: The villager no longer wears the librarian outfit and is again unemployed.

steps.action: Select the Lectern again and right-click the same accessible floor position to replace it. Wait until the villager reclaims it and visibly becomes a librarian again; this generates a fresh set of unlocked trades.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the original lectern position with Lectern selected
steps.success_cue: The lectern is present, the villager has regained the librarian outfit, and the next trade inspection can begin.

steps.action: Repeat steps 16 through 21 as a controlled reroll loop. On each iteration, first open and inspect the fresh trades. If no Density, Breach, or Wind Burst Enchanted Book is offered, close the interface, break the lectern, wait for the profession to be lost, replace the lectern, and wait for the profession to return. On the first iteration where one of those book tooltips is visible, make no trade and stop immediately at step 17.
steps.exact_input: Repeat steps 16-21 until the tooltip inspected in step 17 is Density, Breach, or Wind Burst
steps.success_cue: The Trading screen for a freshly rerolled, untraded librarian remains open, with the pointer hovering over the selected Enchanted Book output and its tooltip visible.

stor.handoff_condition: On the matching reroll, the newly generated novice librarian Trading screen has just been opened and the cursor is hovering over the relevant Enchanted Book output so its tooltip is visible. The world still has no Update 1.21 or Villager Trade Rebalance experimental datapack enabled, and no trade with this villager has been completed. Begin observation without clicking, closing the screen, or changing the villager's workstation.
uncertainties: The report lists both 24w13a and 1.20.5 Release Candidate 1 as affected but does not identify a preferred test version. Release Candidate 1 is recommended because a report comment explicitly confirms reproduction there; 24w13a is an alternative affected version.

The report does not supply a seed, coordinates, game mode, world type, server requirement, or villager acquisition method. The single-player Creative Superflat setup is therefore a practical inference intended to remove unrelated exploration and resource gathering.
The unavailable image attachment may have shown a particular mace enchantment, level, villager tier, price, or interface arrangement. Those details cannot be preserved from the supplied text.
The report says to keep rerolling until a mace enchantment appears but gives no deterministic random seed, probability, or maximum attempt count. The number of loop iterations is therefore unbounded.

The report does not explicitly name the villager profession. A librarian is used because the reproduction concerns a villager offering an enchantment as an Enchanted Book and lectern replacement is the established way to reroll an untraded librarian's offers.

The report does not state whether all three mace-only enchantments demonstrated the issue. Density, Breach, and Wind Burst are all treated as matching targets because those are the three mace-specific enchantments introduced for the affected experimental feature set.
